card_quote: Social use: likes things that can be played out loud with friends. / Narrative: Joined a trivia team after moving cities to meet people; the team's specialist in science and 'weird facts'.
how_read: Game night first: we played rounds one and six at my place with the trivia team, one person reading. Then I kept going on my own over the week, a round or two before bed, mostly the science and psych rounds. Ran out of steam around the end of round eight.

w1_best.why: Monty Hall plus the letters from PhDs. Huge argument at the table, exactly what I want.
Toast actually has physics behind it. Weird-fact gold and it won an Ig Nobel.
Mpemba effect being genuinely unresolved. I liked that it didn't pretend to know.
The sink and Coriolis. Everyone at the table was sure, and everyone was wrong.
The forgetting curve is one guy memorizing nonsense syllables. Wild that my Anki app is built on that.

w1_flat.why: The goldfish page in round eight. Ruined a great question with jargon.
The Franklin kite page, contradicts itself.
Uncertainty principle. True, but nobody at a table can play it.

w1_review.headline: Great questions, answers need a diet
w1_review.body: The questions themselves are really good, especially the psych and science ones, and our trivia team had a great night arguing over them. But the answers are long, academic, and hard to read aloud; we ended up reading just the verdict and the one-line summary. A couple of pages look like errors, including one that says TRUE and then says the opposite. Bottom line: four stars for the questions, two for the editing, would still bring it to game night.

w2_review_first: It's like a trivia night in a book: you vote true, folklore or disputed and then flip. The questions are great for a group, the answers are kind of a slog. Just read the last line out loud and you're fine.

w2_lost.why: Words and phrases round was mostly history and politics, not my thing, so I skimmed it.
Thucydides trap was where I actually put it down for a couple of days.
Goldfish page made me close it in annoyance.

w2_read_aloud.why: Monty Hall gets the table yelling every time.
Butter-side-down toast with real physics behind it.
Rat tails in Hanoi. Gross and great.
Streisand's six downloads, two by her own lawyers. Instant laugh.

w2_cut.title: Do goldfish have a three-second memory?
w2_cut.why: Rewrite it or cut it, it's the worst page in the book.

w2_cut.title: Did Benjamin Franklin fly a kite in a thunderstorm?
w2_cut.why: Its own verdict and text disagree.
More of an essay prompt than trivia.
Habeas corpus is a law-school question.
The second Wald plane question repeats the first one.

w2_book2: If it was the same long answer pages with no quick version to read out loud, I'd stick to trivia apps.
